notes: Now playing shows the storage badge on its title, and its "local file / streaming" line no longer lies about a downloaded YouTube track — the path still starts with yt: while the audio comes off the disk. The badge is sized in em, so it scales with whatever text it sits next to and stops nudging the rest of the row. The Now-playing and Downloads drawers now anchor to the player’s real height instead of a hard-coded offset that only ever matched one layout. Playlist cards in search results answer to right-click, like everything else in that view. Icons everywhere, and a single colour language for storage state. Blue cloud = streamed, needs the network. Green drive = came from YouTube but saved locally, plays offline. Red struck-through cloud = unavailable at the source. Plain local files carry no badge — tagging 1600 rows would turn the signal into wallpaper. The badge now appears on track rows, on the now-playing title, and as a per-playlist summary in the sidebar. Every button in the app has an icon. These three colours sit outside the usual purple accent on purpose: they answer a different question and must not read as selection. Everything the app says is in English again — the last batch had slipped into French. Behaviour is unchanged. Fixed: importing a playlist without "Save locally" no longer empties it. Tracks with no local file were all being hidden, but those stream perfectly well — only tracks the source refuses outright are hidden now, the ones that can neither be downloaded nor streamed. New Stats tab: most and least played tracks, top and least played artists, top albums, total plays and time listened. It required building a play counter first — the history deduplicates by track, so it only ever knew when you last played something, never how many times. Counting therefore starts from zero; past history does not hold this information. A play counts after 30s actually heard (half the duration for short tracks), read from the playback clock so pauses are excluded — flicking through with Next no longer inflates anything. Tracks never played are counted separately from least played. Import dialog: the playlist search is gone — it opens straight on the URL field. Downloads panel: yt-dlp's wall of text is reduced to a short label — a Premium-only video now reads 'Premium only' instead of the id, the repetition and a truncated sentence; the raw message stays in the tooltip. The Activity dot always shows and carries the batch state (purple running, red failed, amber canceled, green all through), and only pulses while something is actually running. The list is split into In progress / Waiting / Failed / Canceled / Saved, failures first. Ctrl+Enter searches in the background: the view stays put, the result parks in Activity and opens on click, and several can run at once without cancelling or overwriting each other. Follow checks appear in Activity with per-playlist progress instead of running invisibly. — Previous fixes still included: removing duplicates now actually saves. The playlist branch called PL._persist, which playlists.js does not export — optional chaining swallowed the call, so the cleanup lived in memory only and duplicates came back on restart. Scrolling no longer stutters: cover art was being re-scanned across every mounted row on each re-slice; it is now deferred and coalesced off the scroll path. Download counts only count what will actually be attempted — already-local and known-unavailable tracks are excluded and reported separately. After a batch, tracks the source refuses for good can be removed on confirmation. Newly downloaded tracks reappear immediately instead of staying hidden until the next restart. Online tracks now carry an icon instead of a text badge, with a distinct colour for unavailable ones. Adding by URL offers to download right away. Playlist Refresh re-fetches titles from the source instead of only rereading the local cache, and a followed playlist can be checked for new tracks on its own.
